$description: The Links — BLUE-STEEL token overlay (round 2, softened brutalist). Stance: blue is the atmosphere, not the accent — every ground, ink, border and grey on the page is one cool hue derived from `palette.screen`, so the whole surface is tinted like the light coming off a simulator projection rather than like a brand colour someone picked. Exactly one warm hue (the ember/amber pendant family, retained verbatim) does every job that needs heat, and forest green is demoted from 'the theme's black' to the one thing it can still mean: the colour of a venue's name.

com.monkeyjumplabs.candidate.register: brutalist, softened per RUN.md 'The softening delta'
com.monkeyjumplabs.candidate.divergenceAxis: palette only — register, layout, IA, copy and data all fixed
com.monkeyjumplabs.candidate.status: PROPOSAL — divergent candidate for a human gate. Not client-approved.
com.monkeyjumplabs.candidate.committedIdea: The room is lit by the screen, so the page is too. This is a single-hue cool-neutral system: eight of the nine neutrals are new values sitting within ±5° of `palette.screen`'s 199°, which means the page has no greys at all — only steel at nine lightnesses. Nothing here is blue because blue is the brand colour; it is blue because that is the temperature of the one light source the venue actually owns. The entire heat budget is one warm hue, spent at full strength in one place.
com.monkeyjumplabs.candidate.whatASiblingWouldNotDo: Refuse to make blue an accent. A sibling will hand blue a job — a button, a band, a highlight — and keep a warm or neutral chassis underneath it. This candidate does the opposite: blue never appears as a coloured element anywhere on the page, because it is the substrate. The only things that are 'coloured' are the ember band, the amber on the dark fields, and the forest green on the two venue names. Restraint is the position, and the risk it takes is that a reviewer reads restraint as absence.

theGapThisDirectionCloses.finding: RUN.md finding 2 — 'the palette cannot render its own brief.' brand-direction.md §5.1 says the venue's signature is 'a warm dark room with one bright screen in it', but the only cool value in the canonical palette, `palette.screen` #2E5A6E, measures 1.81:1 against `palette.night` #0D3520. A simulator projection painted in it is invisible on the dark ground it is supposed to punch out of. Round 1 proposed `palette.screenLight` and did not add it; the brutalist candidate had to fake the projection in `palette.greige`.
theGapThisDirectionCloses.whatThisOverlayDoes: Adds `palette.screenLight` #C3DCE8 under exactly the name round 1 proposed, and measures it: **11.84:1 against `palette.steelNight`**. The Lakeville media slot now renders the brief literally — a near-black cool room, three warm pendant pools, and one bright cool panel that is the brightest thing in the frame — with no substitution and no workaround. This is the one thing this direction can demonstrate that a warm-based sibling structurally cannot.
theGapThisDirectionCloses.secondOrderEffect: Because the ground is now the cool value, the warm accent stops competing with it. In the canonical system ember and screen are both 'a colour on white' and read as two accents. Here ember is the only accent, and screen has become the room.

callOnForestGreen.verdict: DEMOTED, not retired — and given one specific job it could never do before.
callOnForestGreen.was: `palette.forest` #124B2E is declared as the live theme's *black* (--black-hsl: 149.47, 61.29%, 18.24%) and backs 66 sections. brand-direction.md §1 calls it the brand's single strongest colour equity.
callOnForestGreen.isNow: `role.equity.venueName` — the colour of a venue's NAME, and nothing else. It sets the two trust-strip venue links and their underline, and the two `<h3>`s in the 'Two venues' section. It is never a ground, never body ink, never an action, never a rule between sections.
callOnForestGreen.whyThisIsBetterThanKeepingIt: As the theme's black, forest was the substrate — which meant the brand's equity colour could never appear ON a dark field, because forest on its own near-black sibling is 1.36:1. It was everywhere and it meant nothing. In a steel system it is the only non-cool, non-warm value on the page, so the eye reads it as a category: green = this place has a name. That is a direct answer to screen-spec §10.4 ('nothing on the page ever visually says The Links **of Lakeville**') and to brand-direction.md §4.2's endorsement system, and it is the first time the equity colour does work rather than being the floor.
callOnForestGreen.whyThisIsBetterThanRetiringIt: Retiring it spends four years of the only real colour equity the brand has to buy a hue that entered the system this morning. A one-role demotion keeps the equity legible on the page's most-read block (the trust strip) at a cost of zero new values.
callOnForestGreen.theConstraintThisImposes: Forest is a LIGHT-GROUND-ONLY colour in this overlay, and that is arithmetic, not preference: forest vs steelNight 1.67:1, vs steelDeep 1.36:1, vs screen 1.35:1, vs ember 1.36:1 — all far below the 3:1 non-text gate. So on the dark bands (chrome, hero, jobs, footer) the venue name is carried by `palette.amber` instead. Recorded as a rule so nobody reintroduces a green mark on a steel field.
callOnForestGreen.honestCost: Forest appears in exactly six places on this page. A reviewer who wants to *see* the brand's green will find this thin, and that is a fair objection to put at the gate. The counter-argument is that six deliberate appearances of a colour that means something beat 66 sections of a colour that means 'background'.

theOneWarmAccent.value: The ember/amber family, RETAINED VERBATIM from the canonical tokens.json — `ember` #8A400A, `emberHover` #AD500D, `emberActive` #6D3308, `emberMid` #B85718, `amber` #F3B268.
theOneWarmAccent.whyNotANewWarm: Because the argument this candidate makes is that colour must be sourced, and the ember is the only value in the whole system with a measurement behind it: every frame of the existing shoot is red-dominant over blue by +15 to +19, lit by warm pendants over the bar with no daylight (brand-direction.md §2.2). Coining a prettier orange to sit against a new blue would be exactly the invention this direction is arguing against. It also keeps intact the tuning that took real work: ember was chosen as the darkest attractive ember whose *brightened* hover form still clears AA.
theOneWarmAccent.hoverArithmeticReVerified: Against this overlay's new light neutral: `steelChalk` #F3F6F7 on `emberHover` #AD500D = **4.92:1** ✓ (round 1's paper #F7F5F3 measured 4.91:1 — the swap does not cost the hover). `steelChalk` on `emberActive` = 9.09:1 ✓. `white` on `emberHover` = 5.34:1 ✓.
theOneWarmAccent.whyItIsTwoValuesAndNotOne: One warm HUE, at exactly two lightness stops, because a single value provably cannot serve both grounds. brand-direction.md §2.4.2: white text at 4.5:1 forces a fill's relative luminance below 0.183, while a 3:1 boundary against a near-black ground forces it above 0.261 — no value satisfies both. So ember carries the warm on light grounds and amber carries it on dark. That is arithmetic, not a second accent.
theOneWarmAccent.whereTheHeatGoes: One full-bleed ember band (the featured offer + waitlist), the amber on every dark band (eyebrow, score rules, the on-dark CTA fill, the reassurance line, the pendant marks in the media slot), and the ember CTA fills on light grounds. Nothing else on the page is warm.

howThisAvoidsReadingAsColdOrUndesigned: SATURATION, NOT GREY. The classic cool-neutral failure is a desaturated ramp that reads as unpainted UI chrome. This ramp is saturated: 58% at `steelNight`, 56% at `steelDeep`, 41% at `screen`, 45% at `screenLight`, 27% at `steelMist`. Only the two lightest steps drop to 18–20%, where saturation would tint paper. Every dark value on the page is unmistakably blue, not grey.

ONE HUE, NINE LIGHTNESSES. Every new value is within ±5° of `palette.screen`'s 199° (range 195–204°). A cool system reads as undesigned when its neutrals wander in hue; this one cannot, because there is only one hue in it.

THE LARGEST CHROMATIC EVENT ON THE PAGE IS WARM. The ember band is full-bleed and unchanged from round 1. In a page that is otherwise entirely cool it is louder than it was against green, not quieter — one warm field in a cold room is the whole photographic brief, rendered as page structure.

EVERY DARK BAND HAS WARM LIGHT IN IT. Amber sets the hero eyebrow, the score rules, the on-dark CTA, the reassurance line, the footer lockup rules and the pendant marks. The dark bands are not blue rectangles; they are cool rooms with warm light in them, which is exactly what the photographs are.

THE LIGHT END IS BARELY COOL. `steelChalk` #F3F6F7 is 20% saturation at 96% lightness — a hair off white. The page's light grounds do not read as a blue wash; they read as paper that happens to be lit by the same room. This is the single most important restraint: tint the darks hard, tint the lights almost not at all.

GREEN IS STILL THERE, MEANING SOMETHING. The one non-cool, non-warm value on the page marks the two venue names — so the page carries three colour categories (steel = everything, warm = action, green = place) rather than one hue and an accent.

display.rationale: UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1 — the register is fixed for round 2 and the type proposal travels with it. One variable file gives a normal cut for labels and an expanded cut for scoreboard figures, so weight AND width carry hierarchy. Archivo is drawn for high-contrast display at both poster and caption size: a transit board, not an award entry.
display.softeningDeltaApplied: The display weight ramp steps down one notch: round 1's 900 / 800 / 600 becomes **800 / 700 / 600**. The delta permits the peak to come down one step; the ladder is shifted as a whole so the h1-vs-h2 relationship survives instead of collapsing. Scale is unchanged.
display.costOfTheSwap: Unchanged from round 1 and still the most contestable call in the register: a grotesque page face makes the slab 'THE LINKS' wordmark read as a MARK rather than as the same font set larger. Byte budget unchanged (one variable file for one variable file).

body.rationale: RETAINED VERBATIM from the current direction and the live site. Carries tabular figures for hours and bay counts per brand-direction.md §3.2 rule 3.

retiredByThisOverlay.note: Retired from the web build only, as in round 1. It survives inside the drawn wordmark alongside the slab it inherits from.

typefaceProposal.previewApproximation: The wisplet preview loads no network resources. Open Sans is REAL — base64-embedded from public/fonts/open-sans-normal-latin.woff2. Archivo is NOT available and is approximated by the system grotesque stack (SF Pro / Segoe UI / Helvetica Neue) at weight 700–800 with negative tracking. Judge the preview's display type as an approximation; judge this declaration as the proposal.

com.monkeyjumplabs.candidate.photographyHandling: There is no photography in this project and none is faked. Same two moves as round 1, but the first one now works properly: (1) THE DARK GROUNDS ARE THE PHOTOGRAPH'S JOB — the hero is a flat near-black COOL field, because the room is a near-black room lit by a screen; (2) where the playbook demands frames (§3.6), the slot is drawn entirely from palette values that were themselves derived from measurements of the real photography — a steelNight ground, a screenLight panel for the projection at 11.84:1, a screen-blue horizon band inside it, amber points for the pendants — at the real 3:2 aspect, hard-ruled, captioned with the specific frame that is missing per venue. Lakeville's caption says the shoot exists and is not in the repo. **Stillwater's slot is drawn EMPTY AND UNLIT** — a hatched dark field with an unlit frame in it — because that venue has never been professionally photographed and the honest render of 'no frame exists' is not a prettier placeholder. Asymmetric because the truth is asymmetric.

keptVerbatim: `palette.screen` #2E5A6E — kept as a value and PROMOTED from 'informational/status only' to the anchor of the whole neutral ramp. Every new neutral is derived from its hue.
`palette.ember` / `emberHover` / `emberActive` / `emberMid` / `amber` — the entire warm family, values untouched. It is the only measured colour in the system.
`space.sectionY` / `sectionYLg` / `gutterX` / `gutterXLg`, `size.contentMax` / `proseMax` — layout is fixed on this axis.
The whole `typeScale.*` and `tracking.*` and `lineHeight.*` ramp from brutalist.json — the delta forbids changing scale.
`elevation.none` — there are still no shadows on this page.
`motion.duration` 0ms — the delta says nothing about motion, so nothing moves. A 150ms ease is softening past the instruction.
replaced: `palette.night` #0D3520 → `palette.steelNight` #0B1F2A. Reason: the page's black had to become cool for the direction to exist at all. Bonus: white on it is 16.89:1 vs 13.57:1 — the type gets louder for free.

`palette.paper` #F7F5F3 → `palette.steelChalk` #F3F6F7. Reason: a barely-warm off-white contradicts a cool system; the replacement is a barely-COOL off-white at the same lightness, so every ratio it inherits moves by <0.02.
`palette.greige` #E5E1E0 → `palette.steelFog` #DFE5E9. Reason: greige is a warm neutral; fog is the same lightness on the ramp's hue.
`palette.sage` #9CBEAD → `palette.steelMist` #9DB9C6. Reason: sage is a green light field; mist is its steel equivalent and reads BETTER on the new ground (8.19:1 vs sage's 6.71:1 on the old night).
`role.ink.bodyOnLight` forest → `palette.steelInk` #173C4D. Reason: body ink had to leave forest for green to become a category rather than the default.

`role.ink.mutedOnLight` #456052 → `palette.steelMuted` #4A6473. Reason: the old muted is a desaturated green; this is its exact steel counterpart, and it clears AA on all three light grounds (6.25 / 5.75 / 4.91).
addedOutright: `palette.screenLight` #C3DCE8 — the bright cool value round 1 flagged and did not add. This is the direction's whole point.
`palette.steelDeep` #12303F — the second dark, used only inside the media slot's room mass.
retiredByThisOverlay: `palette.emberTint` #F0DCC9 — a warm light field has no home in a cool light ramp, and the offer band is full-strength ember rather than a tint. Flagged rather than silently dropped: if the convergent phase wants a light callout field it should be `palette.screenLight`, which is measured here (steelNight on it 11.84:1, ember on it 5.22:1).

`palette.night` #0D3520, `palette.paper` #F7F5F3, `palette.greige` #E5E1E0, `palette.sage` #9CBEAD — superseded as above. Values are recorded, not deleted, so a convergent merge can see exactly what was swapped for what.

tokenGaps: NO WARNING / UNVERIFIED ROLE — and a monochrome system makes this WORSE, not better. `(hours being confirmed)` is neither an error nor a success; it is unverified data. Round 1 gave it `palette.screen` blue on white, which read as a different KIND of thing because the rest of the page was green. Here blue is the substrate, so a blue badge no longer signals anything by hue. This overlay differentiates it by FORM instead — a 2px screen-ruled caps tag at label size against 3rem hour figures — and records the gap: a real `role.state.unverified` is needed, and it is more urgent in this direction than in a warm one. Proposed but NOT added, because adding a third hue would break the stance.

NO RADIUS / BORDER / ELEVATION / TYPE-SCALE / TRACKING / LINE-HEIGHT CATEGORIES in the canonical tokens.json (RUN.md finding 1, unchanged). All of them are declared below. The convergent phase must promote the winning set into the canonical file.

THE LIGHT RAMP'S ADJACENT STEPS ARE NOT SELF-SEPARATING. white→steelChalk is 1.09:1 and steelChalk→steelFog is 1.17:1. That is fine here and it is deliberate: in this register adjacent light surfaces are ALWAYS separated by a rule, never by a tonal step, so no boundary on the page depends on those ratios. But it is exactly the trap a softer register would fall into, so it is recorded: **do not carry this ramp into a card-and-shadow system without adding a border token to every surface pair.**

COPY GAP, NOT INVENTED: the register still wants the published rate ($35 / hour, real, current through 2026-10-03) on the scoreboard. screen-spec-home.md §7 forbids any string not on the copy sheet and no homepage section carries a price. Flagged for the convergent phase as a one-string copy request, NOT added.

NO BRAND MARK. Unchanged from round 1 and from the canonical file. The wordmark is typeset (Archivo 800, expanded, wide-tracked, caps) and the venue lockup is a typographic rule-and-line treatment per brand-direction.md §4.2. No logo is drawn — that is a commission, not a sprint output.

softeningDeltaAsApplied.radius: `radius.control` 0 → **3px**, bound to buttons, form inputs and the venue-switcher chips ONLY. `radius.surface`, `radius.panel` and `radius.media` stay 0 — panels, cells, the waitlist slab, the quote slots and the image slots are square.
softeningDeltaAsApplied.rules: The visible ruled grid stays. Secondary/internal dividers that were `border.rule` 2px drop to `border.hairline` 1px: the trust-strip venue-name underline and the venue meta row's top/bottom rules. Structural rules (section separators, band tops, the quote-grid head, the venue-row bounds) stay 2px or heavier. `border.score` 4px and `border.slab` 8px unchanged.
softeningDeltaAsApplied.spacing: One step more air INSIDE cells only: venue cell s6→s7, quote slot s5→s6, waitlist slab s6→s7, job row block s6→s7, slot caption s4→s5, stub note s5→s6. `space.sectionY` / `sectionYLg` and the full-bleed band rhythm are byte-identical to round 1.
softeningDeltaAsApplied.type: Display weight ramp shifted one step (900/800/600 → 800/700/600). Sentence case stays. `typeScale.*` byte-identical to round 1.
softeningDeltaAsApplied.unchanged: The scoreboard idea, the labelled cells, the ground inversion sequence (dark → white → dark → white → EMBER → white → dark), hierarchy from weight and scale, and the reassurance copy carrying the loudest treatment on the page.

palette.$description: The cool-neutral ramp. Eight new values, every one within ±5° of `palette.screen`'s 199° hue — so this is one hue at nine lightnesses, not a new palette. Hue range 195–204°. Saturation is deliberately high at the dark end (58% → 41%) and low at the light end (20% → 18%), which is what keeps a cool system from reading as grey while keeping its paper from reading as blue.

steelNight.$description: NEW. hue 201°, L*10.4%, sat 58%. The page's black. REPLACES `palette.night` #0D3520. white on it 16.89:1, steelChalk 15.55:1, steelMist 8.19:1, amber 9.15:1, screenLight 11.84:1 (all AA ✓). Not pure black — anti-slop rule 1.

steelDeep.$description: NEW. hue 200°, L*15.9%. The second dark. Used ONLY as the room mass inside the media slot. white on it 13.81:1, amber 7.48:1, steelMist 6.70:1 (AA ✓). vs steelNight 1.22:1 — a tonal mass, never a boundary.

screen.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM from canonical `palette.screen`, and PROMOTED. It was 'informational/status only, never action'; here it is the anchor the whole ramp is derived from, and it appears as a ground for the first time (the dark-row hover fill, 2.25:1 against steelNight — perceptible as a band change, and white on it is 7.49:1 ✓).

steelMist.$description: NEW. hue 199°, L*69.6%. Muted text and quiet rules on dark fields. REPLACES `palette.sage` #9CBEAD, which was the same job in green. on steelNight 8.19:1, on steelDeep 6.70:1 (AA ✓). On light grounds it is 1.90–2.06:1 — NEVER on light, exactly as sage was.

screenLight.$description: NEW, AND THE POINT OF THIS CANDIDATE. hue 200°, L*83.7%, sat 45%. The simulator projection — the bright cool thing the palette could never render. This is the token round 1 PROPOSED under this exact name and did not add. on steelNight 11.84:1, on screen 5.25:1, on ember 5.22:1 (AA ✓). As a fill it carries steelNight at 11.84:1 and screen at 5.25:1. NEVER on white — 1.43:1.

steelFog.$description: NEW. hue 204°, L*89.4%. Secondary light field and decorative texture. REPLACES `palette.greige` #E5E1E0 at effectively the same lightness. steelNight on it 13.28:1, steelInk 9.23:1, steelMuted 4.91:1, ember 5.86:1 (AA ✓).

steelChalk.$description: NEW. hue 195°, L*96.1%, sat 20%. The off-white. REPLACES `palette.paper` #F7F5F3 — a barely-warm off-white becomes a barely-cool one at the same lightness, so every inherited ratio moves by less than 0.02. Doubles as the text colour on every dark and every warm fill: on steelNight 15.55:1, on ember 6.86:1, on emberHover 4.92:1, on emberActive 9.09:1 (AA ✓).

white.$description: RETAINED. The page ground, as in the canonical file.

steelInk.$description: NEW. hue 199°, L*19.6%. Body text on light grounds. REPLACES forest in that role. on white 11.73:1, on steelChalk 10.80:1, on steelFog 9.23:1, on screenLight 8.23:1 (AA ✓).

steelMuted.$description: NEW. hue 202°, L*37.1%. Captions, meta, placeholders, sub-rules on light grounds. REPLACES `role.ink.muted` #456052, which is a desaturated green. on white 6.25:1, on steelChalk 5.75:1, on steelFog 4.91:1 (AA ✓ body on all three — this is the step a cool-neutral system usually fails, so it was measured against every light ground it can land on).

ember.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM. The action colour, and the only value in the system with a measurement behind it (brand-direction.md §2.2). white on it 7.45:1, steelChalk 6.86:1, steelFog 5.86:1, screenLight 5.22:1 (AA ✓). As a fill boundary against white 7.45:1 (non-text 3:1 ✓).

emberHover.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM, and RE-VERIFIED against the new light neutral: steelChalk on it 4.92:1 (AA ✓ — round 1's paper measured 4.91:1). white on it 5.34:1. The tuning that made ember survive `hover:brightness-125` survives the palette swap.

emberMid.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM. Focus ring / border only, never text-bearing. vs white 4.76:1, vs steelChalk 4.38:1, vs steelFog 3.74:1 (non-text 3:1 ✓).

amber.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM. The pendant light. DARK FIELDS ONLY: on steelNight 9.15:1, on steelDeep 7.48:1 (AA ✓); on white 1.85:1, on steelChalk 1.70:1 (FAIL — never). Also banned on `screen` as body text (4.06:1) and on the ember band (4.04:1).

forest.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM AS A VALUE, DEMOTED AS A ROLE. No longer the theme's black; now `role.equity.venueName` and nothing else. on white 10.14:1, on steelChalk 9.33:1, on steelFog 7.98:1, on screenLight 7.11:1 (AA ✓). LIGHT GROUNDS ONLY — vs steelNight 1.67:1, vs steelDeep 1.36:1, vs screen 1.35:1, vs ember 1.36:1, all below the 3:1 non-text gate.

clay.$description: RETAINED VERBATIM. Error. on white 7.19:1, on steelChalk 6.62:1 (AA ✓).

rule.$description: The load-bearing category: no cards, no shadows, so RULES carry every boundary. Colour by ground, weight by job (`border.*`).

media.$description: The photo-slot system. Every value is a palette colour chosen because that colour was derived from a measurement of the real photography (brand-direction.md §5.1). The slot is a diagram of the frame's own numbers, never a decorative illustration and never a fake photograph.

slotGround.$description: The near-black room. Measured target: 33–38% of frame near-black, mean luminance 54–74/255.

slotMass.$description: The bar and floor mass. 1.22:1 against the ground — a tonal mass inside an illustration, never a boundary.

slotPanel.$description: THE SIMULATOR PROJECTION — the one bright thing in the frame, and the reason this direction exists. 11.84:1 against the slot ground. Round 1 had to fake this in `palette.greige` because the only cool value in the palette was 1.81:1 on the dark ground.

slotPanelBand.$description: The horizon band inside the projection — the measured 7–8% of saturated pixels in the 210–240° band. 5.25:1 against the panel.

slotPendant.$description: The warm in-frame practical light. Measured: red channel exceeds blue by +15 to +19; no daylight, no flash. 9.15:1 on the slot ground.

slotFrame.$description: The 2px rule around the slot. The slot is always visibly a SLOT.

slotLabel.$description: The caption naming the exact missing frame. 8.19:1 (AA ✓).

slotEmpty.$description: The hatch on Stillwater's slot — drawn EMPTY AND UNLIT, because that venue has never been photographed. 8.19:1 as a hairline on the ground.

display.$description: UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1. Replaces Bitter. Variable grotesque, weight 100–900 and width 62–125 in one file.

numeric.$description: Scoreboard figures only — bay counts and hours — set at expanded width with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums`.

retired.$description: Bitter retired from the WEB BUILD only, as in round 1. It survives in the drawn wordmark.

fontWeight.$description: SOFTENING DELTA APPLIED: the display ramp steps down one notch from round 1 (900/800/600 → 800/700/600). Shifted as a ladder rather than only at the peak, so the h1-vs-h2 relationship survives.

displayPeak.$description: The h1 and the scoreboard figures. Was 900.

displaySemi.$description: Caps labels, eyebrows, table heads. Unchanged.

fontWidth.$description: Only meaningful because the proposed display face is width-variable. Unchanged from round 1.

displayExpanded.$description: Scoreboard figures and the wordmark only.

typeScale.$description: BYTE-IDENTICAL TO ROUND 1. The delta forbids a scale change; the comparison is about colour alone.

radius.$description: SOFTENING DELTA APPLIED, AND THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE IT IS VISIBLE AS A SHAPE. 3px on interactive elements only. Everything structural stays square.

control.$description: Buttons, form inputs, venue-switcher chips. Was 0. Three pixels is the smallest radius that is legible as a decision rather than as a rendering artefact.

surface.$description: Panels, cells, the waitlist slab, quote slots. STILL SQUARE.

pill.$description: Declared explicitly so nobody reintroduces a rounded pill for a status badge. The unverified tag is a square-cornered ruled box.

border.$description: SOFTENING DELTA APPLIED: secondary/internal dividers that were `rule` 2px drop to `hairline` 1px. Structural and section rules stay 2px or heavier. Colour comes from `role.rule.*`.

hairline.$description: Cell dividers, the venue-name underline, the venue meta rows. The last two moved here from `rule` under the delta.

rule.$description: Component boundaries that are still boundaries: inputs, buttons, media-slot frames, the unverified badge, section separators, the quote-grid head, the venue-row bounds.

score.$description: The band separator and the focus slab. The recurring graphic device.

slab.$description: The lead rule above the featured job row and the footer top rule.

elevation.$description: Declared so it can be declared EMPTY. There are no shadows on this page. Depth is ground inversion and rule weight.

space.$description: Section rhythm KEPT VERBATIM. The delta's 'one step more air' applies INSIDE cells only and is expressed at the component level, not by changing the ramp.

motion.$description: Dial setting 1. Hover and focus only. UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1 — the delta says nothing about motion, and adding a transition would be softening past the instruction.

contrastAudit.$description: Every text and non-text pairing this candidate renders, computed from sRGB relative luminance per WCAG 2.1 §1.4.3 (not estimated, not recalled). Body gate 4.5:1; large-text and non-text gate 3:1. NOTHING IN THIS CANDIDATE RELIES ON THE LARGE-TEXT ALLOWANCE. NO PAIRING FAILS.
